definitions: Richard Phillips Feynman (1918-1988) was an American theoretical physicist, known for his work in quantum electrodynamics, nanotechnology, and particle physics.
A crater on the Moon is named Feynman.
A main-belt asteroid, 3744 Feynman, is named after him.
examples: Feynman developed a widely used pictorial representation scheme for the mathematical expressions governing the behavior of subatomic particles, which later became known as Feynman diagrams.
The Feynman Lectures on Physics is a famous textbook.
Feynman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1965.
